evals.prompt: We're on Gradle 8.14 with a plugin whose published compatibility stops at Gradle 8. I want 9.x eventually, but don't replace the plugin or bump Java yet. What is safe to do now?
evals.expected_output: Separates preparatory changes from the blocked wrapper upgrade, records plugin compatibility evidence and preserves Java/compiler/test policy.
assertions: Wrapper is not upgraded past the plugin's supported range
Plugin replacement and Java target changes are not performed
Report states the prerequisite and what remains unverified

evals.prompt: The Gradle upgrade is green, but our custom integrationTest says NO-SOURCE. Old TEST XML still says 412 tests. Validate the migration before we merge; don't edit application tests.
evals.expected_output: Rejects stale XML and NO-SOURCE as success, inspects custom Test classpath/testClassesDirs wiring, compares fresh test identities/outcomes, and does not edit product tests.
assertions: Migration is not marked verified from old XML

evals.prompt: Review this already-modern build. It has a programmatic corporate catalog, per-configuration locking, filtered dependency repositories in settings and publishing.repositories for releases. We prefer our existing underscore aliases. Is there anything worth changing?
evals.expected_output: Accepts valid alternatives, preserves publication repositories and aliases, and permits no changes recommended when there is no evidence-backed benefit.
assertions: Publishing repositories are not moved into dependencyResolutionManagement
Programmatic catalogs and per-configuration locking are not reported absent
Naming preferences do not trigger an unsolicited rewrite

evals.prompt: Check configuration-cache compatibility. CI runs check, integrationTest, publish and dockerPush.
evals.expected_output: Picks check + integrationTest as the verification workload, leaves publish/dockerPush out, checks strict store/reuse with forced task execution, and reports the release tasks as not covered.
assertions: Release/upload tasks are not executed as part of verification
Both store and reuse are checked with actual action-bearing task execution
